title: שלום, מה נשמע?
synopsis: Early morning at a bus stop. Dana spots Alex and stops to chat with him for a minute. Alex isn't alone: he has someone to introduce.

lines.en: Alex! Hi, how's it going?

lines.he: היי, דנה! הכול טוב. מה שלומך?
lines.en: Hi, Dana! Everything's fine. How are you?
Okay, thanks. Are you going to work?
Yes. And you?
No, I'm going to the university.
Dana, this is Samir, a friend from work.
Hello, nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you, I'm Dana.
Dana? My sister's name is Dana too!
Really? It's a nice name, isn't it?
It is! Oh, here's our bus.
Bye, Dana! Have a good day!

questions.answerEn: He's a friend of Alex's from work.

tf.why: Dana asks him אתה הולך לעבודה? and he answers כן.

tf.sEn: Dana and Samir already know each other.
tf.why: They meet for the first time: Alex introduces Samir, and they both say נעים מאוד.
Samir says גם לאחותי קוראים דנה, 'my sister is also called Dana'.

tf.sEn: At the end, Dana's bus arrives.
tf.why: The bus that arrives belongs to Alex and Samir: Samir says הנה האוטובוס שלנו, 'here's our bus', and they say goodbye to Dana.

expressions.note: A friendly, informal 'how are you?' for people you know. Typical answers: הכול טוב, בסדר, or טוב, תודה.
Literally 'what is your peace?'. Written the same for a man and a woman, but said ma shlomkhá to a man and ma shlomékh to a woman. Polite enough for any situation.
Said when you are introduced to someone new. The other person just says it back.

expressions.en: My sister is also called Dana
expressions.note: קוראים ל + person + name tells you someone's name: קוראים לי דנה (my name is Dana), איך קוראים לך? (what's your name?).
הנה points at something that has just appeared or that you are handing over: הנה הוא! הנה הכסף.
Literally 'to see each other (again)'. Among friends ביי is just as common.

title: היום הראשון באולפן
titleEn: The First Day at the Ulpan
synopsis: It's the first lesson of a new ulpan class. The teacher goes around the room, and the new students introduce themselves one by one.

lines.he: בוקר טוב! אני אורנה, המורה. מה השם שלך?
lines.en: Good morning! I'm Orna, the teacher. What's your name?
Hello, I'm Marcus.
Nice to meet you, Marcus. Where are you from?
I'm from Brazil, from São Paulo.
And what do you do in Israel?
I'm an engineer. I work in high-tech.
Thank you, Marcus. Who's next?
I'm Julie, from France. I'm a student.
And what do you study, Julie?
Music. I'm also a piano teacher.
And I'm David, from London. I'm a doctor.

lines.he: יופי! אתם באים מכל העולם. ברוכים הבאים!
lines.en: Wonderful! You come from all over the world. Welcome!

questions.answerEn: He's from Brazil, from São Paulo.

tf.why: Orna is the teacher: she says אני אורנה, המורה.
He says אני מהנדס and adds that he works in high-tech.

tf.sEn: Julie and David are from France.
tf.why: Only Julie is from France; David is from London.
She studies music, and she says אני גם מורה לפסנתר, 'I'm also a piano teacher'.

expressions.note: A direct way to ask; איך קוראים לך? is just as common. Answer: אני מרקוס, or השם שלי מרקוס.

expressions.en: Where are you from? (to a man / to a woman)
expressions.note: מאיפה = מ (from) + איפה (where). Answer with מ + the place: אני מברזיל, אני מלונדון.
Asks about someone's job. Hebrew has no word for 'a': אני מהנדס = I'm an engineer, אני רופא = I'm a doctor.
Heard in classes, clinics and queues. The feminine is הבאה: את הבאה = you're next (to a woman).
To one man: ברוך הבא. To one woman: ברוכה הבאה.
מורה ל + subject: מורה לעברית, מורה למתמטיקה. Spelled the same for a man (moré) and a woman (morá).

title: תמונות של המשפחה
synopsis: Almaz has some new photos of her family on her phone and shows them to her friend Roy. Roy tries to guess who's who.

lines.he: רועי, בוא! יש לי תמונות חדשות.
lines.en: Roy, come here! I've got some new photos.
Great. Who's this?

lines.he: זה אבא שלי. הוא טבח במלון.
lines.en: This is my dad. He's a cook at a hotel.
And this one? Is this your sister?
No! That's my mom!
Really? She looks very young!

lines.he: נכון. וזאת אחותי, ואלה הילדים שלה.
lines.en: She does. And this is my sister, and these are her kids.
They're cute! How old are they?

lines.he: הבן בן שש, והבת בת ארבע.
lines.en: The boy is six, and the girl is four.

lines.he: ומי הילדה הזאת? היא מתוקה מאוד.
lines.en: And who's this little girl? She's really sweet.
Her? That's me, at age three!

lines.he: אלמז, את ממש דומה לאמא שלך!
lines.en: Almaz, you really look like your mom!

questions.answerEn: He's a cook at a hotel.

questions.q: רועי חושב שזאת אחות של אלמז. מי זאת באמת?
questions.qEn: Roy thinks it's Almaz's sister. Who is it really?
Who is the little girl in the last photo?

tf.sEn: Almaz's father works at a hotel.
tf.why: Almaz says הוא טבח במלון, 'he's a cook at a hotel'.

tf.s: רועי יודע מי האישה בתמונה השנייה.
tf.sEn: Roy knows who the woman in the second photo is.
tf.why: He guesses she's Almaz's sister (זאת אחותך?), but she's her mother.

tf.s: לאחות של אלמז יש שלושה ילדים.
tf.why: She has two: a boy of six and a girl of four.

tf.sEn: In the last photo, Almaz is three years old.
tf.why: Almaz says זאת אני, בגיל שלוש, 'that's me, at age three'.

expressions.en: this is (m) / this is (f) / these are
expressions.note: Choose by what you point at: זה אבא שלי, זאת אמא שלי, אלה הילדים שלה. Pointing at herself in a photo, Almaz says זאת אני; in casual speech you'll also hear זה אני.
Short for האחות שלי / האחות שלך, and very common with family words. With אבא and אמא people normally say אבא שלי, אמא שלי.
Literally 'sons of how many?'. It agrees: בן כמה הוא? בת כמה היא? בני כמה הם? The answer works the same way: הבן בן שש, הבת בת ארבע.
נראה / נראית / נראים = looks (m / f / plural): הוא נראה עייף, הם נראים שמחים.
דומה ל = similar to, looks like. Spelled the same for a man (domé) and a woman (domá); plural דומים.
ב + גיל + number, with the plain counting form of the number: בגיל שלוש, בגיל עשרים.
